# rlsbl confidential

Resolve the confidential-term hits of what this repository publishes. The confidential-term list (Projects/CONTEXT/confidential/terms.toml.age under the home directory, encrypted with age to the identity in ~/.age-key.txt, and decrypted in memory only; a missing list has no terms) names terms that must not appear in anything public. A release (and selfdoc's publishing) scans what it would push or publish, reports every hit at once, each with an id, its location, and the text around it, and refuses while a hit has no resolution in .strictmetadata/confidential-hits/resolutions.toml. Each hit is judged by the agent: one it is at least 70% certain is a false positive is recorded with judge-false-positive; every other one goes to the owner, who has the text fixed or approves publishing it with approve-hit. The release records the resolutions it used in the version's release archive. A hit id names the list entry, the matched text, and the words after it, so the same phrase has the same id wherever it appears, and a resolution resolves it everywhere. The `confidential-terms` check reports the hits of the next push.

## confidential judge-false-positive

Record the agent's judgment that a confidential-term hit is a false positive, in .strictmetadata/confidential-hits/resolutions.toml, and commit it with the Autogenerated trailer. --hit names a hit the next push or a tracked file of this repository carries (the ids the confidential-terms check and the release's refusal print); any other id is refused, naming the hits there are. --certainty is how certain, in percent, the agent is that the hit is not confidential, from 70 to 100: a hit judged less certain is the owner's to resolve, with approve-hit or a fix. --reason is one line, and is refused when it carries a confidential term, since the file is committed. The recorded location has every confidential match redacted. A hit resolved already is refused.

**Effect:** mutating

### Flags

| Name | Short | Type | Presence | Env | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--hit` |  | str | required |  | The hit's id, as the confidential-terms check and the release's refusal print it |
| `--certainty` |  | int | required |  | How certain, in percent, the agent is that the hit is a false positive: 70 to 100 |
| `--reason` |  | str | required |  | Why the hit is not confidential, in one line without the term |

## confidential approve-hit

Record the owner's approval to publish a confidential-term hit anyway, in .strictmetadata/confidential-hits/resolutions.toml, and commit it with the Autogenerated trailer. Only the owner approves a hit: pass --approve-consequential only when the owner approved this specific hit, and give the owner's own reason in --reason (one line, refused when it carries a confidential term, since the file is committed). --hit names a hit the next push or a tracked file of this repository carries; any other id is refused, naming the hits there are. A hit resolved already is refused.

**Effect:** mutating · **consequential** (prompts before running; `--approve-consequential` skips)

### Flags

| Name | Short | Type | Presence | Env | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--hit` |  | str | required |  | The hit's id, as the confidential-terms check and the release's refusal print it |
| `--reason` |  | str | required |  | The owner's reason for publishing the hit, in one line without the term |
